extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, communications teams, PR agencies, and anyone writing/distributing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for crafting and distributing press releases that attract journalist coverage, are easy to use, and measurable — covering story construction, required elements, distribution strategy, pitfalls, and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with a hook / Strong hook in first 30 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Always lead with a hook; strong hook in first 30 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open immediately with the most newsworthy element to capture attention; the first ~30 words should make the reader care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote adds insight (not fluff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quotes to add insight instead of filler language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes that provide perspective, context, or a unique viewpoint reporters can use; avoid generic praise or empty platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline SEO-optimized
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize headlines for search engines and readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that balance readability and keyword relevance to help with discoverability and AI/SEO use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-pronged distribution: targeted pitches AND wire services
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute via targeted pitches AND wire services as part of a two-pronged approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online distribution for SEO/AI visibility and personalized outreach to spark coverage and follow-up; combine both rather than relying on only one channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness / Passes the 'so what' test
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights a newsworthy announcement clearly; newsworthy (passes 'so what' test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly explain what the announcement is and why it matters now — if it doesn't answer 'so what', it likely won't earn coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why it matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly explain the significance and impact of the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect the news to outcomes, trends, or audience concerns so journalists can quickly understand relevance and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to target audience clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows relevance to specific audience clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor messaging to the beat and interests of the outlets or journalists you're targeting; make the target audience explicit where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy for journalists to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the release easy for journalists to use in their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear facts, quotable material, and assets so reporters can quickly repurpose content without extra legwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information visible and complete
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information must be visible and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear, accessible media contact (name, phone, email) so journalists can reach someone without searching; missing contact info is a common fatal flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate present
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a boilerplate company description at the end of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise background paragraph about the company/organization to give context for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia provided in shared folders
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multimedia (videos, headshots, logos) in shared folders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-resolution assets and make them easy to download via a shared folder or link so journalists don't have to request visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and pre-answer likely questions / Provide pre-vetted facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the need for follow-up questions by anticipating journalist needs and providing pre-vetted facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data, background, and clarifications reporters commonly ask for so you reduce friction and speed up coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer expert availability / Expert available for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer and make available experts for follow-up interviews or clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who is available, their role, and how to contact them; offering on-the-record experts increases pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a targeted distribution plan focused on relevant journalists and outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the specific reporters, beats, and outlets most likely to cover the story rather than broad, untargeted lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized outreach component
rubrics_metrics.description: Include personalized outreach as part of distribution to spark coverage and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize pitches to the outlet/beat and explain why the story matters to that reporter rather than sending generic copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance over reach / Quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize relevance (quality) over sheer reach (quantity) when choosing recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A smaller, well-targeted list of relevant journalists is more valuable than mass-distribution to uninterested contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match release to beat / Customize for outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the release to the reporter's beat and customize content for the outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust emphasis, examples, or data to align with a beat's focus (e.g., tech, health, local) to improve fit and pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overhyping (undermines trust)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overhyping claims or embellishment that undermine credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be factual and restrained; sensational language can damage trust and reduce long-term media relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic mass distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid sending generic mass distributions that aren't targeted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass blasts often get ignored and can harm reputation; prefer targeted pitches and selective wire use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement plan in place / Basic metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a measurement plan and track basic metrics (opens, engagement, coverage pickups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track email opens and engagement and whether outlets picked up the story as core indicators of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced measurement metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track advanced metrics such as which journalists responded, follow-up questions asked, click-throughs, and audience reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these metrics to refine targeting, evaluate spokesperson effectiveness, and attribute coverage to specific tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe embargo discipline when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an embargo, communicate clear embargo terms and ensure all recipients respect the timing to maintain credibility and coordinated coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of common mistakes: overhyping, generic mass distribution, missing contact info, no multimedia, no clear news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit releases for these issues before sending; they are frequent reasons journalists ignore or delete releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a distribution and measurement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for both how you'll distribute the release and how you'll measure outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete PR plan pairs targeted distribution tactics (personalized outreach + wire) with specific metrics to evaluate success and follow-up.
